useFor: A record's state, category or rank as a short word in a tone, read beside a title, in a table cell or in a line of text.

combineWith.how: A row's state in a column of its own, in words as well as a tone.
In .card-head-right, the record's state beside its title.
In .list-meta at the end of a row, the state of the person or record the row names.
The AI label is a button that opens a popover saying where the value came from.

notFor.text: A filter or a pick the user can remove
What an agent is doing right now
A condition of the whole page
A count on a navigation link

useFor: A thing the user put there and can take away — an applied filter, a chosen person, a label on a record — with its remove button, in a set that wraps.

combineWith.how: The toolbar changes the filters; the chip set under it says what is applied, then Clear all.
Every choice ticked in the facet panel repeats as a chip above the results.
Each pick in a multiselect field is a chip inside the field's box.
An .avatar--sm inside the chip for a chosen person.

notFor.text: A state that reflects the data
A choice between a few views or settings

useFor: Who did something or who is involved — a picture, initials or an icon — as one person, a group or a pair, with their presence and whether someone is acting as them.

combineWith.how: An avatar, a name and a second line is a .list-row with .list-main; there is no person class.
An .avatar--sm inside a chip for a chosen person.
The user widget's .user-avatar, ringed while an administrator acts as someone.
A .badge--warn that says Acting as in words beside the ring.
A person's access in the next column of a table, changed from a value trigger.
A group conversation in a list takes .avatar-pair, so the names stay in one column.

notFor.text: An agent rather than a person
What a person did, in order
